title: gpu-pool-degradation-field-journal
content:
Summary:

This is a working field journal for the GPU pool degradation that started on 2025-01-11 ~02:03 UTC and had recurring slowdowns through ~2025-01-12 22:00 UTC. The intent: capture signals, quick experiments we ran, attempted mitigations, rough hypotheses, and next actions for a fuller postmortem. This is not final — notes to self and collaborators below.

Impact (user/business):
- Dedicated customers on pool 'mx-ded-2' saw increased P95 token latency from ~180ms to 850-1200ms for generation requests.
- Error rate (500) spiked from ~0.1% -> 3% during worst window (02:10-03:50 UTC).
- Autoscaling failed to add sufficient nodes in two surge episodes due to throttled scale-up decisions (see timeline). Some tenants experienced queueing and timeouts.

Initial signals and dashboards checked:
- pool_health.free_gpus dropped from 12 -> 2 (alert)
content_continued_2: \n- kv_cache.evictions/sec increased sharply for top-5 tenants (tenant-id masked)
content_continued_3: \n- node_cpu and node_gpu_utilization were normal on candidate nodes; contention looked infra-level on host VMs (driver stalls observed)
content_continued_4:
Timeline (compressed):
- 2025-01-11 02:03 UTC: First pager; routing SLO alerts show rising latency on mx-ded-2
- 02:06: Pager acknowledged by on-call (Aisha). Slack incident channel created (#ops-2025-01-11-gpu-slow)
content_continued_5: \n- 02:10-02:40: Rapid P95 climbs. Triggered automated scale-up (configured min-burst=2). New nodes launched but did not accept allocations for 6-8 minutes intermittently (kube-svc flapping seen)
content_continued_6:
- 03:00: Observed high kv_cache_thrash for tenant T-42 (heavy long-context reranking workload). Suspected noisy neighbor: long KV sequences causing memory pressure and eviction waves. Began soft isolation: moved T-42 to quarantine pool (manual routing override), immediate partial relief for other tenants
- 03:30: Throttle and eviction events persisted, but overall error rate reduced after quarantine
- 04:00: Autoscaler misconfig suspected: hysteresis and backoff intervals set too high (scale-down cooldown 20m, scale-up backoff 8m), resulting in underreaction to rapid traffic surges. Noted historical PR that changed defaults: PR #4586
- 05:20: Temporary mitigation: lowered scale-up backoff to 45s and enabled extra burst capacity (policy override) for mx-ded-2. Latency improved slowly
- 07:00: Night shift handover. Left runbook TODOs for daytime investigation
- 2025-01-11 15:10: Secondary spike after internal load test + natural traffic. Found kube-svc endpoint churn on new hosts; kube-proxy conntrack exhaustion observed
- 2025-01-12 09:30: Repro experiment: replayed tenant T-42 workload in staging with current autoscaler config -> caused alloc retries and KV eviction cascade
- 2025-01-12 18:20: Applied inhibitor: enforced per-tenant KV cache quotas in pool (alpha flag) to limit thrash, observed reduction in eviction/sec
- 2025-01-12 21:30: Declared incident stabilized. Follow-up actions planned

What we ran and quick diagnostics (commands / artifacts):
- kubectl get pods -n pool-mx-ded-2 -o wide -> found frequent CrashLoopBackOff on prewarm-agent on some hosts
- curl /healthz on prewarm-agent -> occasionally 502 from kube-proxy, matching conntrack evictions
- nvidia-smi dmon and dcgm-exporter readings -> driver timeout spikes concurrent with alloc retries
- Allocator logs (grep AllocationFailed) -> consistent backpressure with 'no free device' even though nodes reported GPU free; suspect driver-level stalls
- jq '.[].eviction_reason' kv_cache_metrics.json -> majority 'kv_cache_capacity' then 'tenant_oom'
hypotheses:
Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Noisy tenant triggers KV cache thrash + eviction storms -> causes allocator churn (hot-cache amplification). Evidence: T-42 replay reproduced thrash in staging; eviction/sec correlated tightly with alloc failures.
2) Autoscaler backoff/hysteresis misconfig prevents rapid scale-up during short bursts, causing sustained queueing. Evidence: change in defaults in PR #4586; scale-ups happened but were delayed due to backoff; reducing backoff improved responsiveness.
3) conntrack / kube-proxy limits reached on new nodes causing control-plane flapping and delay for newly launched nodes to accept allocations. Evidence: kube-proxy logs show conntrack rejections; increasing net.netfilter conntrack_max removes symptom in short-term.
4) GPU driver/firmware intermittently stalls under combined long-KV + heavy IO workloads, making GPUs appear free but unallocable. Evidence: driver timeout spikes in DCGM aligned with latency incidents but not with 100% gpu_util. Needs more repro.
immediate_mitigations:
Immediate mitigations applied (what worked vs didn't):
- Quarantined noisy tenant (T-42) -> immediate partial relief. WORKED
- Lowered scale-up backoff -> measurably reduced P95 in next surge. WORKED
- Raised conntrack_max on nodes -> helped kube-proxy stability but is bandaid. PARTIAL
- Forced node restart for 3 problematic hosts -> resolved some driver hang symptoms. WORKED but disruptive
- Enabled per-tenant KV cache soft quota (alpha) -> reduced eviction cascade in hour-long test. WORKED (needs broader testing)
runbook_gaps:
Runbook gaps discovered (notes):
- No clear playbook for quick per-tenant quarantine routing; current process manual and error-prone. Need API/CLI to route specific tenant to quarantine pool with TTL.
- Autoscaler config defaults too conservative for bursty LLM workloads; no documented knob guide for SRE on-call.
- Lack of signal tying KV cache evictions to allocator health in a single dashboard; correlation took too long.
- No dedicated alert for kube-proxy conntrack approaching danger threshold on new nodes.
proposed_followups:
Proposed follow-ups / action items (owners tentative):
- Create 'tenant-quarantine' CLI route and API (owner: Diego) -> implement server-side route that forces specific tenant->quarantine pool for N minutes. (JIRA-INFRA-1001)
- Autoscaler tuning RFC: propose new defaults for backoff/hysteresis for dedicated pools with LLM workloads; include warm-up preallocs. (owner: Sofia) (CONFLUENCE-234)
- Add a composite dashboard: kv_cache_evictions/sec, allocator.failed_alloc_retries, pool_free_gpus, kube-proxy_conntrack_count. (owner: Evan)
- Implement per-tenant KV quotas as GA feature with metrics and circuit-breaker on eviction rate. (owner: Eng-ML + SRE)
- Write runbook steps for on-call: quarantine flow, fast scale-up override, node restart checklist, conntrack mitigation (sysctl tweak), and criteria for declaring incident stable. (owner: Aisha)
- Follow-up hardware/firmware validation with vendor for observed driver timeouts (owner: Infra HW team)
open_questions:
Open questions / research items:
- Why did some nodes report free GPU but allocator still failed? Driver hang vs container runtime issue? Need deeper SDE trace during repro.
- Should we change model of KV cache from shared per-pool to per-tenant isolated shards? Cost/benefit analysis required.
- Is the conntrack issue unique to our base AMI/kernel? Can we bake kernel tuning into node image?
- Can autoscaler simulation harness include KV eviction feedback to predict allocator blowups?
cheatsheet:
Notes to future on-call (quick cheatsheet):
- If P95 > 600ms and allocator.failed_alloc_retries > 100/min -> check top tenants by kv_cache.evictions/sec
- To quarantine tenant (manual): PATCH routing service /routing/pool_override {tenant: T-xx, pool: quarantine, ttl: 30m}
- Quick scale-up override: set autoscaler.override.burst=+2; reduce backoff to 45s for pool mx-ded-2
- If kube-proxy conntrack > 80% of tracked_max -> increase net.netfilter.conntrack_max by 30% and restart kube-proxy on affected nodes
appendix:
Appendix (logs & snippets):
- allocator snippet: "AllocationFailed: device busy; driver timeout after 15s" (repeated)
- kube-proxy: "conntrack: table full, dropping packet" at 02:24
- kv_cache metric line example: tenant=T-42 evictions=345 rate=5.8/s
raw_todos:
Raw thoughts / TODOs for full postmortem:
- Build better reproduction harness that combines long-context KV-heavy workload + bursty traffic to exercise allocator + autoscaler path end-to-end
- Add SLO for allocator error rate and include it in incident severity scoring
- Consider autoscaler fast-path for short spikes: pre-allocated 'hot' nodes that can be instantly used (prewarm with some VM reservation)

End of field journal. Will convert into formal incident writeup once SRE engs return and we have deeper traces.

-- Aisha
(adding Diego/Sofia/Evan as collaborators for follow-ups)
